issues.display_title: Issue #592: Consolidate Profile Follower and Following Flows
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Consolidate Profile Follower and Following Flows

  • Date: 15-10-2026
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Consolidated the user relationship query pipeline across ProfileFollower and ProfileFollowing in src/Action/V1/Users/, eliminating over 300+ lines of duplicated authorization, lookup, block checking, and response serialization logic:

  1. Shared Pipeline Helpers (src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers.go):

    • resolveProfileRelationshipTarget: Validates URL parameters, role permissions (user, viewer, my-user), user visibility (ResolveUserVisibility), target user database records, deactivation status, viewer token validity, and mutual block states.
    • getFollowedStatusMap: Resolves followed status via UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs in a single batch query for users, safely returning empty map for viewers.
    • buildRelationshipItems: Formats follower/following items, applying role-dependent followed state and hide flags for blocked users.
    • sendRelationshipResponse: Standardizes JSON response envelopes with transparent AES encryption when ec=true.

  2. Refactored Handlers:

    • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go: Reduced from 218 lines to 54 lines.
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollowing.go: Reduced from 218 lines to 54 lines.
    • Preserved profileFollowerQuery and profileFollowingQuery function signatures to retain complete compatibility with existing dry-run SQL tests.

  3. Automated Unit Tests (src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers_test.go):

    • Added unit tests for:
      • TestRelationshipStringValue: Safe interface string conversion.
      • TestGetFollowedStatusMapViewerReturnsEmpty: Verifies viewer bypass and empty user IDs handling.
      • TestBuildRelationshipItemsFollowers: Verifies follower payload generation across user, viewer, and blocked states.
      • TestBuildRelationshipItemsFollowings: Verifies following payload generation.

2. Files Updated

  • src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers.go: New shared relationship pipeline helpers.
  • src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers_test.go: 4 unit test suites for relationship helpers.
  • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go: Refactored to delegate to shared helpers.
  • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollowing.go: Refactored to delegate to shared helpers.

3. Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Unit Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Users/...
# PASS: TestProfileFollowerQueryAppliesSearchOnlyInSearchMode
# PASS: TestProfileFollowerRejectsInvalidRole
# PASS: TestProfileFollowingQueryAppliesSearchOnlyInSearchMode
# PASS: TestProfileFollowingRejectsInvalidRole
# PASS: TestRelationshipStringValue
# PASS: TestGetFollowedStatusMapViewerReturnsEmpty
# PASS: TestBuildRelationshipItemsFollowers
# PASS: TestBuildRelationshipItemsFollowings
  • Area: User Relationship Queries (Feeds API)
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollowing.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers_test.go
  • Date: 15-10-2026

1. Problem

ProfileFollower.go (218 lines) and ProfileFollowing.go (218 lines) contained over 85% duplicate code across their handler implementations:

  1. Identical URL parameter unescaping (username and usernameFullname).
  2. Identical role authorization checks (user, viewer, my-user).
  3. Identical user visibility resolution (ResolveUserVisibility) and cache timestamp handling.
  4. Identical target user lookup (WHERE username = ? AND banned = false).
  5. Identical self-profile access gating for my-user.
  6. Identical deactivated user filtering against target users.
  7. Identical viewer role token validation.
  8. Identical mutual block checks for authenticated users.
  9. Identical batch followed status resolution using UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs.
  10. Identical response envelope formatting and optional AES encryption (ec=true).

Only the underlying database query table/foreign-key mapping (followers.follower_id vs followers.user_id) and the JSON wrapper key (followers vs followings) differed.

2. Scope

  1. Extract Shared Relationship Helpers (src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers.go):

    • Implement resolveProfileRelationshipTarget(c *fiber.Ctx, search bool) (*profileRelationshipContext, bool):
      • Unifies URL unescaping, role validation, visibility resolution, DB user lookup, block checks, and pagination calculation into a single reusable pipeline.
    • Implement getFollowedStatusMap(role, myUserID string, userIDs []string) (map[string]bool, error):
      • Safely resolves batch followed status for authenticated users while returning an empty map for viewers without unnecessary DB queries.
    • Implement buildRelationshipItems(itemKey string, users interface{}, userIDs []string, followedUserIDs map[string]bool, relCtx *profileRelationshipContext) []map[string]interface{}:
      • Dynamically maps scanned ProfileFollower and ProfileFollowing structs to standard client response shapes, applying followed and hide flags correctly based on role and block context.
    • Implement sendRelationshipResponse(c *fiber.Ctx, messages, resultKey string, dataList []map[string]interface{}, relCtx *profileRelationshipContext) error:
      • Standardizes 200 OK JSON responses and ec=true AES payload encryption.

  2. Refactor ProfileFollower.go and ProfileFollowing.go:

    • Streamline both handlers by delegating shared target resolution, followed status mapping, and response packaging to relationship_helpers.go.
    • Preserve existing query helper signatures (profileFollowerQuery and profileFollowingQuery) for 100% test compatibility.

  3. Automated Unit Tests:

    • Add unit tests in src/Action/V1/Users/relationship_helpers_test.go verifying string helper conversions, viewer bypass for batch followed status, and relationship item building for both followers and followings.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route signatures, HTTP status codes, error message strings, JSON response shapes, and AES encrypted envelopes remain completely unchanged.
    • Query filters (search by username/fullname, deactive user exclusion, banned user exclusion) remain identical.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • ~300+ lines of duplicate code eliminated.
  • Unit tests pass with go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Users/....
  • go vet ./... reports zero issues.

issues.display_title: Issue #593: Consolidate Timeline Feeds Query and Response Pipeline
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Consolidate Timeline Feeds Query and Response Pipeline

  • Date: 15-10-2026
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Consolidated the database query building, content visibility, Elasticsearch enrichment, and response formatting pipeline across MostPopularPost, TimeLinePostRecent, and TimeLinePostJustForYou in src/Action/V1/Posts/, eliminating ~270+ lines of duplicate code:

  1. Shared Pipeline Architecture (src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go):

    • TimelineFeedConfig: Struct containing metadata (Messages), allowed include fields, default SQL select columns, dynamic query extension callback (BuildQuery), and role-based sorting callback (Order).
    • fetchAndRenderTimelineFeed: Centralized executor performing pagination, visibility checking, database query composition, Elasticsearch counter enrichment, bookmark status resolution, and response generation.
    • sendTimelinePostResponse: Centralized HTTP response formatter handling field filtering (filterTimelinePosts) and optional AES encryption (ec=true).

  2. Refactored Handlers:

    • MostPopularPost.go: Reduced from 117 lines to 32 lines.
    • TimeLinePostRecent.go: Reduced from 118 lines to 32 lines.
    • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go: Reduced from 138 lines to 35 lines.

  3. Automated Unit Tests (src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go):

    • Added unit test suites verifying string helper conversions and timeline feed response generation.

2. Files Updated

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go: Added TimelineFeedConfig, fetchAndRenderTimelineFeed, sendTimelinePostResponse.
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go: Added tests for response generation and helper conversions.
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go: Refactored to delegate to shared pipeline.
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go: Refactored to delegate to shared pipeline.
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go: Refactored to delegate to shared pipeline.

3. Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Unit Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Posts/...
# PASS: All unit tests pass cleanly

  • Build:

    go build -v ./cmd/...
# PASS (0 errors)
  • Area: Feeds / Post Query Pipeline
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go
  • Date: 15-10-2026

1. Problem

The three core timeline feed endpoints in src/Action/V1/Posts/ (MostPopularPost, TimeLinePostRecent, TimeLinePostJustForYou) contained ~370 lines of code with over 85% duplicate logic:

  1. Identical context setup: timestamp resolution, pagination (limit/offset), role and encrypt extraction.
  2. Identical content visibility resolution (ResolveContentVisibility) handling deactivated users and blocked posts.
  3. Identical user bookmarks retrieval from Redis (ListBookmarksUser).
  4. Identical base query on views_timeline_post filtering visibility = 'public' and post_type != 'video360'.
  5. Identical dynamic field selection handling for the include query parameter with essential slug enforcement.
  6. Identical exclusion filters for blockedPosts and notInEncrypt (excluded users).
  7. Identical post count enrichment via Elasticsearch batch lookup and bookmark status resolution (enrichTimelinePosts).
  8. Identical response formatting, include-field filtering (filterTimelinePosts), and AES encryption handling (ec=true).

Only the sorting order, customized WHERE clauses (e.g., following filters for JFY), and response message text differed between them.

2. Scope

  1. Extend src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go:

    • Define TimelineFeedConfig encapsulating endpoint message, allowed include fields, default select string, custom query builder callback, and role-based ordering callback.
    • Implement fetchAndRenderTimelineFeed: A generic, reusable pipeline orchestrating the entire lifecycle (visibility check, query building, execution, enrichment, and response).
    • Implement sendTimelinePostResponse: Standardized JSON response formatting with transparent AES encryption support.

  2. Refactor Feed Handlers:

    • MostPopularPost.go: Streamlined to declare configuration and order by score_mostpopular DESC, slug.
    • TimeLinePostRecent.go: Streamlined to declare configuration and order by created_at DESC.
    • TimeLinePostJustForYou.go: Streamlined to declare configuration with following list filtering for users and dual ordering (score_mostpopular and score_timeline).

  3. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Add unit tests in src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go verifying string conversion helper, response generation, and timeline post data formatting.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route signatures, query parameters (include, ec, sl, page), HTTP status codes, and response structures remain completely identical.
    • Sorting orders, user-following filters, and Elasticsearch counter lookups function identically.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • ~270+ lines of duplicate query and formatting logic eliminated.
  • All unit tests pass with go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Posts/....
  • go vet ./... reports zero issues.
